clue.text: Aria from bird of peace — like this number?

parts.note: the dove is the traditional emblem of peace
so can mean in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A question about whether a song about the peace bird resembles the piece being performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dove sono' is the Countess's aria in Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro; 'number' doubles as a musical item in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous operatic solo sung by the Countess in Mozart's Figaro, so an example of the category named.

clue.text: Thomas Ken put in fruit without hesitation

indicators.note: Ken is put in, placed inside the fruit after it has been trimmed
without tells us to drop the hesitation from the fruit

parts.note: a tangerine is a small citrus fruit
er is the sound of hesitation
taken as written, a man's name

explanation.surface: A man called Thomas Ken placing something inside a piece of fruit without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Ken looks like one person's name (he was a real bishop and hymn writer), but the definition is just 'Thomas', and Ken is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas is the title character of the children's railway stories, a small blue steam locomotive known by this full name.

clue.text: Clown turning up on a high with a scrubber

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the clown's word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a fool is a jester or clown
H is the abbreviation for high, as on a weather map or pencil grade

explanation.surface: A clown, feeling up and elated, appears with a cleaning brush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses FOOL to LOOF in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This dried gourd fibre is used as a bath sponge for scrubbing the skin, so it is a kind of scrubber.

clue.text: Listener's home, the grave?

parts.note: a listener is an ear, the organ that listens
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Asking whether the place where a listener lives is the tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listener's home' reads as the ear's nest; 'grave' looks like a noun for a tomb but is the adjective meaning serious. 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone serious and solemn in manner, so they are synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: A term pet used to adapt old style

indicators.note: the letters are used, put to work in a new order, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone describing a pet name as a way of fitting in with a bygone manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' tells you to rearrange A TERM PET; 'old style' says the definition is an archaic verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to temper, moderate or modify something so it suits, which is to adapt it.

clue.text: Truancy where being 4 was important for the interment of a small cake

parts.note: a bun is a small round cake
interment is burial, the act of burying

explanation.surface: A fanciful account of skiving that ends with a little cake being buried.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest, Algernon invents a sick friend called Bunbury as an excuse to escape duties; 'being 4' (Earnest) points to the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon's habit of inventing an invalid friend to dodge social duties is a form of truancy, named after that imaginary friend.

clue.text: See 25
Drink and drink, missing a round — pass one

indicators.note: missing says the round thing is left out of the second drink

parts.note: cocoa is a hot chocolate drink
O is round in shape
a col is a mountain pass
A is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A drinker passes on one round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like a verb (to skip a round) but is a mountain pass, and 'one' is the article A.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known brand of fizzy soft drink, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Intrude force in go-slow?

annotationWithheld.why: Intrude force in go-slow? (6) TRUDGE: the only parse reads 'Intrude' as IN + TRUDE, so the IN is both cut from the word and the signal to put G (force) inside the rest; one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Weirdo gives horse to king

parts.note: gee or gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An eccentric hands over a horse to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for an odd, socially awkward person, close in meaning to an oddball.

clue.text: Knuckle down to working one's ____ to the ____

definitions.meaning: a knuckle is a joint in the bones of the hand's digits
the idiom 'work one's fingers to the bone' means to labour very hard; its two missing words give the answer

explanation.walkthrough: 'down to' is a link with a hint of 'knuckle down', meaning to work hard, which ties the surface to the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The knuckle is a joint formed by the small bones of a hand digit, so the answer names the bone itself.

clue.text: Guardian articles a model among a lot of newspapers?

definitions.text: Guardian articles a model among a lot of newspapers?

parts.words: Guardian articles a model among a lot of newspapers?
parts.note: the Guardian newspaper holding itself up as one exemplary member of the whole press corps

explanation.surface: A newspaper boasting that its pieces set the standard among the press.
explanation.walkthrough: The press is called the fourth estate, after the clergy, nobility and commons; the Guardian, where the puzzle appeared, is one paper among many.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional name for the press and journalists collectively, ranked beside the three classic estates of the realm.

clue.text: One with a great future? Rats!

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the word for a celestial body, going up in a down entry, spells this exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone hailed as a coming talent, and an exasperated exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: in a down entry 'rising' reverses, so STAR rising makes RATS, the clue's last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person tipped for success who is quickly becoming prominent is said to have a bright future ahead.

clue.text: Don't let one drink to the foregoing

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in sips
the answer just before this one in the grid, 12/25, is a name for the press

explanation.surface: Advice against letting someone raise a glass to what was said earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the foregoing' refers to the previous across answer, the fourth estate, meaning the press. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something back and not allow it to come out, as when you stop yourself letting a sneeze escape.

clue.text: The first 45 minutes slightly burns the pictures in a residential area

parts.note: three quarters of an hour is 45 minutes, so the first three quarters of the word for sixty minutes
to singe is to burn slightly
the Tate is a group of London art galleries, home to many pictures

explanation.surface: In a football match's first half, the sun scorches the paintings hanging in a suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 45 minutes evokes a football half but means three of HOUR's four letters, HOU. The Tate is a famous set of British art galleries. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned development of many homes built together is a residential district, often council-built in Britain.

clue.text: Mr Bean, raised outside prison, provides 22across 15s

indicators.note: outside means the reversed name goes around the prison word
raised, in a down clue, means the name is read upwards

parts.note: Sean Bean is an English actor, so Mr Bean's first name is Sean
a cell is a room in a prison

explanation.surface: The comic character Mr Bean, lifted up around a jail, supplies engine parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Not Rowan Atkinson's comic Mr Bean but the actor Sean Bean, whose first name is needed; 'raised' reverses it in this down entry to NAES. 'provides' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These streamlined casings on an aircraft enclose its engines, so they are engine housings.

clue.text: Liberal use of writing?

indicators.note: making use of the letters freely signals that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about generous employment of the written word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the adjective 'generous', but it is the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This system of raised dots read by touch is a form of writing for blind people.

clue.text: Lion and mule entangled on the floor

indicators.note: entangled says the letters of the two animals are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A lion and a mule wrestle together on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a joining word, not part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard-wearing sheet covering is laid on floors, so it is what you find on the floor.

clue.text: Ice for a short time in Italy

parts.note: a berg is a mass of floating ice
mo is short for moment, a short time

explanation.surface: Ice that lasts only briefly in an Italian setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Lombardy in northern Italy, so something found in that country.

clue.text: Road on Riviera or in southwest England, as they say?

indicators.note: as they say means as it is spoken, so a word that sounds the same

parts.note: things from Cornwall, in southwest England, are described as Cornish

explanation.surface: A road found on the Mediterranean coast or in Britain's far southwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's southwest tip; its adjective is said much like the French word for a cliff road.
explanation.definitionFit: A road cut along a cliff face, especially the famous coast roads of the French Riviera.

clue.text: Not necessary to expose 10 toes

indicators.note: to expose the letters is to lay them out afresh, here signalling rearrangement

parts.note: the number 10 written as the letters I and O, which look like its digits

explanation.surface: No need to bare all ten toes.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is read as the letters IO, not as a cross-reference to 10 across; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serving no practical purpose is superfluous, so not needed at all.

clue.text: See 2
Milk from the next or the next but one house

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of clue words that follow

explanation.surface: Getting milk from the house next door or the one after that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk' is the verb, to exploit for money; the letters sit in 'next or the'. 'the' before it and 'next but one house' complete the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk someone is to drain money from them, as to obtain it by threats or force.

clue.text: Stairs — outside stairs — as removed and destroyed at dawn

indicators.note: outside means the first set of stairs goes around the rest

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs

indicators.note: destroyed says what remains of the second stairs is broken up and rearranged
removed tells us the two letters of as come out of the second stairs

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Stairs are pulled out and demolished at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: The removal leaves TIRS; 'destroyed' rearranges that into IRST, which sits inside FLIGHT after its first letter. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest light of the day, when the sun first appears, is daybreak.

clue.text: After 24 down, the 12 means freedom

definitions.meaning: the month following the summer month that answers 24 down
the Fourth (12 across) of this month is American Independence Day, celebrating freedom

explanation.walkthrough: The second part leans on 12 across: the Fourth of the answer is the US national holiday marking independence.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the calendar month following June, and its fourth day is the American Independence Day holiday.

clue.text: I keep a French month

indicators.note: keep means hold inside, so one word contains the other

parts.note: je is French for I
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Someone holding onto a French calendar month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs both pieces: the French for 'I', JE, keeps the French for 'a', UN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the sixth month of the calendar year, an example of the category.

clue.text: Terrible tease at first part of 3 concerned with 15

indicators.note: terrible means badly made, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the first three letters of 3 down are LOO, a lavatory, which is also called the gents

explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges TEASE AT into ESTATEA; 'first part of 3' is the start of LOOFAH (3 down), whose synonym is GENTS. 15 is HOUSING.
explanation.definitionFit: These people sell and let homes for a living, so they deal professionally with housing.

clue.text: Sugary affair heard to come back after being booed?

indicators.note: heard means we want a word that sounds like the one described

parts.words: to come back after being booed
parts.note: a throwing stick that comes back is a boomerang; after the boo is taken from it, the remainder is said

explanation.surface: A sweet romance that returns after being jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' suggests BOOMERANG; 'after being booed' strips BOO from it, and the remaining MERANG, 'heard', sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This light dessert of whisked egg white and sugar is a very sugary confection.
